text:
Jo (Designer): quick sketch: compress roles table rows, move SSO toggle to the top-right of org settings panel. keeps invite flow buttons visible. cc @Liam
Liam (Product): i'm concerned about discoverability of the SSO toggle if it's not near auth settings. why top-right?
Jo (Designer): idea was contextual: when editing org-level roles, SSO enforcement is a common quick action. top-right acts like a global action anchor, similar to billing.
Nina (Frontend): implementation question: top-right sticky would need to be keyboard-focusable and in DOM order before the panel content for SR users. we can't rely on visual placement only.
Caro (Security): regulatory note: toggling SSO should surface the impact on existing invites and session expiry. maybe a warning inline: "Enabling SSO will expire non-SSO sessions within 24h"
Ben (PM): yes, and we should add a soft-confirm with link to audit log entries so admins can see which users might be affected.
Jo (Designer): mock copy draft: "Enable SSO enforcement — all users will be required to authenticate via your SSO provider. Active non-SSO sessions may be invalidated." short and clear?
Liam (Product): tweak: "may be invalidated" -> "will be signed out within 24 hours" more definitive.
Caro (Security): prefer "may be signed out" unless we can guarantee 24h; legal prefers softer language.
Nina (Frontend): accessibility: add an aria-describedby pointing at the warning and ensure the confirm button is the primary action, with keyboard focus trapped until decision.
Jo (Designer): on the roles matrix: proposed compact row shows role name, assigned count, last updated, and a small "inherited" badge. clicking the assigned count opens a drawer with audit trail links.
Ben (PM): drawer for audit trail is good. make sure it links to audit log filtered by role action so admins can jump straight to relevant entries.
Nina (Frontend): for performance, lazy-load the audit entries and show a placeholder skeleton. large orgs will cause heavy queries otherwise.
Caro (Security): audit log filter should include invite events, role assignment changes, and SSO toggles. retention policy note: some customers need 1 year retention — show a retention label on the drawer header.
Jo (Designer): UX nit: if the assigned count is zero, hide the drawer affordance and show "no users" text. keeps clutter down.
Liam (Product): copy for invite CTA inside matrix: "Invite members to this role" vs "Add user" — which is clearer?
Ben (PM): "Invite members to this role" clarifies email invites rather than provisioning. prefer that.
Nina (Frontend): keyboard nav: tab order should go Role name -> Invite CTA -> Assigned count -> kebab menu. ensure screen reader announces "Assigned 12 users, open audit drawer" when focused.
access-bot: Accessibility checklist added to thread: https://internal/checklists/a11y-rbac (automated) :lock:
Caro (Security): tiny but important: kebab menu should include "View role audit" and "Export assignments" — both must be permission-gated.
Jo (Designer): i'll update the figma and add the drawer prototype flows + copy variants. will bring to next sync for validation.
Liam (Product): thanks — please include a small user-testing script: 3 tasks around enabling SSO and checking impacted users. we'll do two moderated sessions.
Ben (PM): i'll coordinate with Ops to ensure the backend flags for lazy-loading audit queries are ready.
Jo (Designer): noted. i'll push updates and tag everyone.
